t: You're at St Bartholomew's Hospital, known as Barts, a teaching hospital in the City of London. It was founded in 1123 by Rahere, and today it is run by Barts Health NHS Trust. Plenty of lives began and ended here. The filmmaker and artist Derek Jarman died here, as did the poet Lionel Johnson and the pathologist Ernest Kennaway. The Soviet spy John Vassall was born here, and so was the comedian Nick Helm. It is a place where the City's long history and ordinary human moments meet.
